ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, slightly to the right of the center, there is an oblique line intersecting a horizontal line. The angle labeled 120° is located below the horizontal line and on the left side of the oblique line; angle 4 is located below the horizontal line near the same intersection point and on the right side of the oblique line. Reasoning: The 120° angle and angle 4 are adjacent angles, and their non-common sides lie on the same horizontal straight line, therefore they form a pair of linear angles, and their sum is 180°. So ∠4 = 180° - 120° = 60°.

raw_record.question_text: Find the measure of $\angle 4$ in the figure.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram around the intersection where the slanted blue segment crosses the horizontal blue line near the center-right. The angle marked 120° lies below the horizontal line on the left side of the slanted segment, and angle 4 lies below the horizontal line on the right side of the same slanted segment. Since these two adjacent angles form a straight line, they are supplementary: angle 4 = 180° - 120° = 60°.
